analyst_view.overall: Early view: Both sides arrive in poor shape: Milan have lost three of four European games under Ruben Amorim, who said after the 2-0 home defeat to Ferencvaros that the team is 'not ready to be competitive on two fronts', while Sunderland lost 2-0 at home to Dinamo Zagreb and were reported bottom of the Premier League. Milan sit 28th and need points to reach the play-off places, so this matters more to them than to Sunderland on seven points.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean slightly lower: Milan managed only two shots on target against Ferencvaros and Sunderland struggled to get shots away against Dinamo Zagreb, so neither attack is in form. Milan have also had injuries in attack this autumn, with Goncalo Ramos and Samuel Chukwueze reported out in October.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.7 corners. Nothing I found points clearly either way; Sunderland had most of the ball against Zagreb without much end product, and Milan's wide options were thinned by Alexis Saelemaekers' ankle surgery.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean a little higher: Milan are under pressure at home and a frustrated side chasing a result tends to pick up bookings, and Sunderland are without Trai Hume through a yellow-card ban, which hints at an edgy campaign. The referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots. Milan had 15 shots against Ferencvaros, so volume is not their problem; quality is, which keeps me close to the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean lower because both sides have been wasteful: Milan put two of 15 shots on target against Ferencvaros, and Sunderland drew few saves in their home loss to Zagreb.
